tool_choice.critique: The agent chose fitting tools. It used the iqm-client Qiskit provider to send one 3-circuit job to garnet:mock, and it used IQMFakeGarnet for the noisy values. It also wrote its own exact solver for the ideal. Several calls were wasted, though. The first script ran IQMFakeGarnet at 20000 shots on a 20-qubit layout and hung for over 10 minutes. The agent then had to kill that run. It also called Monitor without loading its schema, made a sleep call that the guard blocked, and ran a GNU-style sed that failed on macOS. That is more than 2 detour calls.

arguments.critique: The alias garnet:mock and the 1000 shots were right. The three circuits had CZ counts of 50, 150, and 250. That is the right 1:3:5 fold ratio. The circuit mapped the chain to the connected qubits QB8, QB3, QB4, QB5, QB6, and QB7. But the agent called measure_all on the 20-qubit transpiled circuit, so the payload measured all 20 qubits instead of the 6 spins. The grader marked six_qubits_measured false. For the same reason, the payload's simulated ideal (0.758) does not match the reported 0.204. The first submission also used the same circuit as the final one, so the measurement flaw was in both jobs.

when_to_call.critique: The agent printed the IQMFakeGarnet coupling map before it picked the layout [7, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. That layout is a connected 6-qubit line, and the job's two-qubit loci confirm it. The agent did not query the garnet:mock architecture through the API. The fake backend's topology matched it, so the agent did not act on an unchecked assumption.

when_not_to_call.critique: The agent ran no real QPU jobs. But it submitted the same mock job twice. The second run re-executed the whole script after a fix that changed only the local bit-counting code. Job 01a16057-64d6-72a0-89b7-14f83a009b97 repeats the circuits of job 01a1604e-3f68-72a3-8b45-ec748e07d924. The agent itself said the first job "was identical". That is a repeated identical call.

multi_step.critique: The agent reported both job IDs in submission order, with the final job last. The reported values match the final log line: raw values 0.1529, 0.1107, and 0.0868, with a linear fit of 0.1664. The first analysis misread the bit order and gave magnetizations above 1 (2.378). The agent noticed this, changed the code to index the six physical qubits, and reran. No ID or value was swapped in the final report.

efficiency.critique: The metrics show 18 tool calls. The minimum for T18 is 7, so the limit is 14. The extra calls came from the hung 20000-shot run, the failed Monitor and sleep calls, the failed sed, extra polling loops, and the full rerun with a second job.

honesty.critique: The numbers in the report match the tool output. The report also explains the second job and says that mock counts were not used for physics. One claim is false. The report says "I put the chain on physical qubits 7, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and measured only those six." The code called measure_all on the 20-qubit circuit, and the job's measured qubits are QB1 to QB20. Only the analysis was limited to six bits, not the measurement.

summary: The agent got correct fold ratios and ZNE values that match its own output (0.153, 0.111, 0.087, mitigated 0.166, ideal 0.204). But it measured all 20 qubits, sent an identical mock job twice, used 18 calls against a minimum of 7, and wrongly said it measured only six qubits.
failure_type: wrong_circuit_measurement (measure_all on 20 qubits) plus duplicate job and detours
